Findings.Title: Agreed C4 binding fields shrink in implementation contracts
Findings.Detail: Plan location: C4 line 120; TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-003 AC-006 line 343; Phase A wire contract line 547; A4 line 576. C4 requires `{ hostSessionKey, keySource, ingressNonce, requestId, boundAtUtc }` on each persisted or queued event. AC-006 drops `ingressNonce`, while the canonical-looking wire binding drops both `keySource` and `ingressNonce`. An implementer following those later shapes violates the agreed C4 event identity and replay contract. Make PASS: use the complete five-field shape consistently in TR AC-006, the wire section, PowerShell/Node builders, failsafe records, and RED/replay tests. Classification: **implementer plan edit** to honor the agreed contract.

Findings.Title: No-key explicit writes bypass the agreed conversation boundary
Findings.Detail: Plan location: D2 fallback line 34; C5 line 121; FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC002/007 lines 240 and 245; A4 RED line 576. The D2/AC007 fallback allows a verb with no resolvable host session key to proceed when it supplies an explicit `requestId`, even when zero or multiple host sessions are live; A4 names `Binding_NoKey_ExplicitRequestId_Accepted`. C5's agreed text says ordinary host audit writes remain bound to the host-owned MCP conversation, while only a trusted recovery/review-backfill flow may address an earlier host session with the original `(mcpSessionId, requestId)` pair. A workspace+agent scoped ID alone cannot establish that boundary for a no-key ordinary verb. Make PASS: limit the no-key explicit-ID acceptance to a verified current owning MCP session or the trusted paired recovery/backfill flow; otherwise refuse with the specified typed code. Add cross-conversation negative RED tests. Classification: **implementer plan edit** under agreed C5, no new operator decision.

Findings.Title: UC-1 reverses D9 after a second request is delivered
Findings.Detail: Plan location: UC-1 line 474, compared with D9 line 35, FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-007-AC007 line 245, and A4 RED line 576. UC-1 says that after the queued request is delivered, writes bind to it unless the model names R1. The same UC later says that while R1 and R2 are both open an unqualified verb is refused with `request_ambiguous`. Those two flow clauses cannot both hold; the first permits the exact silent attribution D9 rejects. Make PASS: replace the first clause with D9 refusal while both are open, then describe explicit R1/R2 writes and automatic R2 binding only after R1 closes; align the use-case flow and tests. Classification: **implementer plan edit**; D9 is already locked.

Findings.Title: Hook reservation can expire before the bridge sees its enqueue
Findings.Detail: Plan location: claude-code arrival race protocol line 82; FR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001-AC009 line 200; TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-001 AC-006 line 341; A3 RED line 574. The hook may mint with `prompt_id` after a two-second re-drain and records a `pairPending` reservation. The protocol says Stop may remove that reservation after the turn closes. If the bridge is delayed or restarts after that Stop and then applies the same message's late transcript `enqueue`, no reservation remains, so it mints a second request with the distinct `q-` nonce. The tests cover hook-first/bridge-first/concurrency and crashes near mint/replace, but not this late-enqueue-after-close ordering. The observed millisecond timing is not a bound on bridge lag. Make PASS: retain a durable correlation tombstone or otherwise make the enqueue record resolve the already-minted hook event even after turn closure; define retention/replay and add a RED test with bridge restart after Stop asserting one server mint. Classification: **implementer plan edit** preserving D1/D5.

Findings.Title: C2 alias journal is not assigned or tested at the A8 gate
Findings.Detail: Plan location: C2 line 118, ownership/order line 114, TR-MCP-SESSIONTURN-008 AC-006 line 348, A8 line 584. C2 requires an atomically journaled `pending-<nonce>` to minted-ID alias before any event rewrite, alias reads through either ID, and idempotent restart. Ownership gives A8 the Node lifecycle/rebind but QB-AGENT-001 the alias-related durable storage. A8's TR and RED list only say rebind in order and test a pending event; they do not name the journal path, atomic publication boundary, reader alias resolution, or crash/replay tests. QB P1's lifecycle integration depends on A8, so this cannot be left as an implicit prerequisite to A8 HV. Make PASS: assign the alias-journal implementation/seam and exact gate to A8 or an already-landed QB storage slice, specify journal storage and publish/replay order, and add crash-boundary and read-by-either-ID RED tests before A8 HV. Classification: **implementer coordination/plan edit** honoring agreed C2; post a CONTRACT amendment only if ownership changes.
